newsitem.title: UK: UK property survey sees broad-based rental recover.
newsitem.headline: UK property survey sees broad-based rental recover.

text.p: Underlying returns from the institutional property market improved 9.6 percent in 1996 -- exactly in line with their long-term average, an Investment Property Databank (IPD) report said on Friday.
It said a gentle acceleration in rental growth, the first in six years, to 3.1 percent was key to this.

"While heavy over-renting diluted much of the immediate impact of this increase on capital values, the rental recovery was instrumental in halting the upward creep in equivalent yields, which had depressed returns in 1995," the report said.
IPD said contributions from active management were all positive and its portfolio benchmark had risen to 10.4 percent.

A strong income return of eight percent, the first increase in rental values in six years and a virtually unchanged all-property yield were the main influences on property returns over the year, it added.
The survey found that for the fourth year running, property returns were uniform across the market, with a rise in rental values in all three sectors and generally flat yields.
Retail property recorded the highest returns of 11 percent while industrial properties showed a return of 10.2 percent.
IPD said standard shops in central London showed returns of 16.0 percent, just ahead of retail warehouses with returns of 15.4 percent. Office parks' returns were 10.5 percent over the year.

The research company also said that although an average year for the property sector, it was the second best performing asset in Britain, beaten only by UK equities with total returns of 16.8 percent.
It said property returns now compared favourably with those on most other assets on a three-year view.

IPD said there had been a small net investment in property of 0.5 billion stg in the funds it monitors. It said total spending on purchases was 3.0 billion stg, with total capital expenditure rising to 4.6 billion stg, compared with 3.8 billion stg in 1995.

Disposals were broadly unchanged on 1995 at 4.1 billion stg, showing that in line with recent years investors monitored by IPD "were net sellers of standing investment properties in 1996 and were using net proceeds to fund developments and improvements".
"By far the most favoured sector was retail warehouses, which saw net investment of 600 million stg, equivalent to 14.2 percent of portfolio value," IPD said.
London and southern offices recorded a net disinvestment of 436 million stg.
